text: BULLCHIP BANTER: DUHS AT THE ROUNDTABLE
The carved round table. Nine days to the midterms. The coffee is cold. The Duhs have the floor.

alt: DuhBurro: (tapping the microphone) Is this thing on? Good. Folks, prices are up 3.7 percent from a year ago. Who did that? Not us.
DuhElefante: (bangs the gavel) Not us either. Let the minutes show we were out of the room.
Hooter: The data show prices rose 0.6 percent in September alone. Gasoline led. Core inflation, without food and energy, is 2.6 percent.
DuhBurro: Core? Nobody eats core. Nobody drives core.
DuhElefante: For once, my colleague is right. Strike that from the minutes.
BadAsk: Diesel is $6.28 a gallon. A year ago it was $3.62. That's up 73.4 percent. Every truck, tractor and freight train burns it. So who pays?
DuhBurro: The consumer pays. Which is why we're blaming the other side.
DuhElefante: And we're blaming yours. See? Bipartisan.
BitMe DaBear: Brent crude is $115.2 a barrel, against $60.7 a year ago. Earlier this month it touched $130.2. The Iran war began in February. Does diesel care who's in charge?
DuhBurro: Then we need lower interest rates. Before November 3rd.
DuhElefante: Seconded. All in favor? (gavel) Unanimous.
Capo DaWolf: (from the far end of the table) You vote. We price. The Fed holds the short rate near 3.8 percent. The 10-year Treasury yields 5.2 percent. That one is ours.
DuhBurro: Who elected you?
Capo DaWolf: Nobody. That's why we're still here. Mortgages run 7.4 percent. The federal debt is $39.5 trillion. The interest bill tops a trillion dollars a year. More than defense.
DuhElefante: A trillion for interest? Who borrowed all that?

text: (DuhBurro points at DuhElefante. DuhElefante points at DuhBurro.)

alt: Hooter: The ledger says both.
Boss Hog: (grinning) Don't stop now, fellas. Nine days to go. Who's handing out the checks?
DuhBurro: A diesel rebate!
DuhElefante: A gas tax holiday!
Capo DaWolf: Paid for with what? More bonds? Yours.
LePhewy: (sliding into an empty chair) Gentlemen. I have a coin that hedges inflation, diesel and elections. Guaranteed.
BadAsk: Bitcoin is about $81,800. A year ago it was about $107,200. Some hedge.
LePhewy: Past performance... (and he's gone)

Bucky DaBull: Here's what nobody at this table says out loud. Retail sales are up 6.3 percent from a year ago. Unemployment is 4.2 percent. The S&P 500 sits near 7,700. The economy keeps building while Washington argues.
DuhBurro: Exactly what I said. Thanks to us.
DuhElefante: Exactly what I said. Thanks to us.
Hooter: One more date. October's inflation report comes out November 10th. One week after the votes are counted.
DuhBurro: (long pause) Can we move the election?
DuhElefante: Can we move the report?
BadAsk: So who really sets the price of a gallon of diesel, a mortgage, a Treasury bond? The voters on November 3rd? Or DaCabal, every morning at eight?

text: (Off mic. The Duhs clink coffee cups.)

alt: DuhBurro: Same time after the election?
DuhElefante: Same trough.
